title: Grain Harvest Management Scheme
summary: Learn about the Grain Harvest Management Scheme (GHMS), which allows heavy vehicles to exceed regulated mass limits when transporting certain grains.
intro:
The NSW Grain Harvest Management Scheme (GHMS) promotes the safe and productive movement of grain.

Under the scheme, heavy vehicles may exceed the regulated total mass limits by up to 5% when delivering some cereals, oilseeds and pulses. This applies from the farm to participating grain receivers in participating NSW council areas.

To operate a heavy vehicle under the GHMS, you do not need to enrol or pay an application fee.

Find out about the Grain Harvest Management Scheme.
who_can_apply: Operating a heavy vehicle delivering cereals, oilseeds, or pulses from a farm to a participating grain receiver in a participating NSW council area.
what_you_need: None (No enrolment or application fee is required).

faqs.q: What does the Grain Harvest Management Scheme (GHMS) allow?
faqs.a: The GHMS allows heavy vehicles to exceed regulated total mass limits by up to 5% when delivering cereals, oilseeds, and pulses.
It applies from the farm to participating grain receivers in participating NSW council areas.

faqs.q: Do I need to enrol or pay a fee to operate under the GHMS?
faqs.a: No, you do not need to enrol or pay an application fee to operate a heavy vehicle under the GHMS.
